findings.body: The filtered `all(...)` assertions here and at line 152 also pass when the expected entries are absent. Deleting Alpha, Beta and Gamma instead of retaining them as `done` would pass both these assertions and the later disappearance check. Likewise, missing Other, Backup or New issue entries pass the preservation assertion. Item 4 requires these records to remain with the specified statuses and `closed_by`, and retained history feeds Learn the traps. Assert that every expected entry exists before checking its fields, or compare against the complete expected list.

findings.body: When the default branch has a hotspot, a checked-out Git branch such as `fix/bug_123` or `forge/upgrade/v2` makes this comprehension call `repo.read_state` with an invalid Forge item name. `read_state` calls `state_path`, which refuses these names (src/forge/repo.py:431–445), so `forge next` exits 1 without printing its report. The existing worktree loop already excludes these names at nextstep.py:164–165. Apply that same validation here for both prefixes so unrelated Git branches remain ignored.
findings.title: Validate fix branch names before reading their states
